title: Exact Randomization Inference for Binary Outcomes in Mostly Paired Matched Sets
banked_reason: The acknowledged routine 4^q exhaustive extension supplies a useful reference implementation but no literature-grounded consequence commensurate with novelty_target=field; its assessed tier is letter.
gap_reasons: The acknowledged routine 4^q exhaustive extension supplies a useful reference implementation but no literature-grounded consequence commensurate with novelty_target=field; its assessed tier is letter.
The draft’s width-only XP enumeration does not rule out FPT; its hardness attempts and bounded interval scan establish neither a lower bound nor an interval theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery produced a sound exact near-pair enumeration theorem and reference-algorithm plan, but independent review assessed its 4^q extension as routine and letter-tier. A non-identical pivot tried to lift matched-triple context reversals into a quantitative width-only streaming lower bound; repetition lost the required preference direction and polynomially many type-count summaries remained. The implementation, Chiba-supplement comparison, and brute-force benchmarking remain useful follow-on work, but no supported field-tier theorem survived.
tldr: Can an explicit-unit, mostly paired binary experiment have its entire worst-case exact randomization-tail curve, exact confidence set, and a labeled maximizing completion at every attainable ATE computed by one polynomial-space streaming pass? The proposed incremental note specifies an exact reference evaluator with a \(4^q\) exceptional-unit factor and a proved bit bound, so small or sparse experiments with a few larger matched sets can be analyzed without randomization simulation.
gap: Global exact stratified ATE inversion is known, and the pair law is known, but the inspected sources do not supply one label-preserving streaming output contract for all \(N+1\) inclusive two-sided tails, reduced rationals, confidence-set membership, witnesses, and a uniform \(O(4^q(N+L+1)^8)\) bit bound. Chiba’s listed SAS supplement could not be inspected, so priority over its code remains provisional.
fill: Give a precise finite-summary extension of Zhang’s pair law, streaming exceptional enumeration, exact rational endpoint accounting, label-preserving backpointers, a reference implementation and differential tests, plus a proof of correctness, bit time, space, and finite-randomization coverage. This is an incremental algorithm/reference contribution.
